TxFieldPreimageV1, TxOrderFieldFragmentV1, and TxOrderFragmentBundleV1 were the counted per-item publication fragment and its off-chain plan. #587 deleted all three with the receipt chain: under docs/spec/midgard-tx.md §4 a field commitment is one flat blake2b-256 over the whole preimage, so a per-item Merkle opening has nothing to be checked against and the mint policy that consumed these was unsatisfiable for any payload whose commitments were the §4 flat hashes of real material. It was not unsatisfiable outright — the opening is checked against the commitment the payload's own compact declares, so a payload declaring counted roots could satisfy it and have a material-bearing order authenticated. The tx-order mint's all-empty verify_order_material closes that residual by construction. The §8 successor is a different artifact, not a renamed one — FieldPreimageCertificateV1 over §8.4 chunks — and #589 will add its registry row when the certificate ships; no such row exists yet.

canonicalForms.name: Script-integrity hash preimage over the required script-language views
canonicalForms.kind: definite CBOR array of two items whose blake2b-256 digest is the script-integrity hash
canonicalForms.wireRepresentation: 82 || definite_bytes(redeemer_tx_wits_hash) || script_language_views, where script_language_views is the canonical CBOR map keyed by the language tag in ascending numeric order: a102<view> for PlutusV3 alone (key 2), a11880<view> for MidgardV1 alone (key 0x80 = 128), and a202<view>1880<view> for both. <view> is the single frozen canonical cost-model view shared by PlutusV3 and MidgardV1. The empty required set is not an empty map: it is the fixed digest blake2b_256(0xf6), i.e. the CBOR-null root 01f4b788593d4f70de2a45c2e1e87088bfbdfa29577ae1b62aba60e095e3ab53.
canonicalForms.versionPolicy: MIDGARD_V1_CANONICAL_COST_MODEL_VIEW is frozen equal to the Harmonic PlutusV3 default cost model for the initial protocol, so both language keys carry the same view bytes while remaining separately addressed. The redeemer witness hash must be exactly 32 bytes and the language bitmap must be in 0..3; anything else fails closed on both sides.
exactFields: 0: redeemer_tx_wits_hash (32-byte blake2b-256 of the redeemer witness preimage)
1: script_language_views (CBOR map from language tag to canonical cost-model view, keys ascending)
canonicalForms.constructorTagsNotApplicable: The script-integrity preimage is a plain CBOR array containing a CBOR map, not a Plutus Data constructor. The language identities live in the map keys instead: 2 for PlutusV3 and 128 for MidgardV1.
canonicalForms.boundary: Transaction body script_integrity_hash, recomputed on L1 by the validation machine immediately before the CEK phase.
canonicalForms.binding: expected_script_integrity_hash rejects a redeemer hash that is not 32 bytes, a negative bitmap, and any bitmap above 3; the validation machine compares the claimed script_integrity_hash against this recomputation and emits an exact rejecting successor on mismatch.
canonicalForms.persistence: Persisted inside the canonical Midgard transaction body as the script_integrity_hash field and therefore inside the transaction id and commitment; recomputed rather than trusted at validation time.

canonicalForms.name: Midgard V1 script-proof Merkle leaf preimage family
canonicalForms.kind: domain-separated blake2b-256 leaf preimages over canonical CBOR fragments
canonicalForms.wireRepresentation: Every leaf is blake2b_256(ascii_domain || fields) where integers use cbor.serialise and byte strings use a definite-length CBOR byte string. The domains are the exact ASCII strings MidgardScriptSourceLeafV1, MidgardInlineScriptSourceLeafV1, MidgardRedeemerLeafV1, MidgardScriptPurposeLeafV1, MidgardSignerLeafV1, MidgardOutputItemLeafV1, MidgardOutputDescriptorLeafV1, MidgardScriptExecutionLeafV1, MidgardScriptContextItemLeafV1, and MidgardResolvedContextItemLeafV1.
canonicalForms.versionPolicy: Leaf domains and field orders are frozen for V1 and are never reset; a new leaf shape requires a new domain string rather than a re-ordering. Language tags admitted by the source and execution leaves are exactly 0, 3, and 128, purpose kinds exactly 0..3, and context collection kinds exactly 0..7.
exactFields: MidgardInlineScriptSourceLeafV1: 0 source_index, 1 script_language_tag, 2 script_hash (28 bytes), 3 script_total_length, 4 item_commitment (32 bytes)

MidgardScriptSourceLeafV1 (reference variant): 0 constant 1, 1 source_key (canonical out-ref CBOR), 2 script_language_tag, 3 script_hash (28 bytes), 4 script_total_length, 5 item_commitment (32 bytes)
MidgardScriptPurposeLeafV1: 0 purpose_kind, 1 purpose_index, 2 script_hash (28 bytes), 3 subject
MidgardScriptExecutionLeafV1: 0 language_tag, 1 purpose_leaf (32 bytes), 2 source_leaf (32 bytes), 3 redeemer_leaf (32 bytes or empty for native scripts)
MidgardScriptContextItemLeafV1: 0 collection_kind, 1 item_index, 2 semantic_root (32 bytes), 3 cbor_length, 4 memory
canonicalForms.constructorTagsNotApplicable: Script-proof leaves are hash preimages built from domain strings and canonical CBOR fragments, not Plutus Data constructors, so there is no constructor tag to pin. The equivalent closed enumerations that the leaves do pin are the language tags 0/3/128, the purpose kinds 0..3, the context collection kinds 0..7, and the resolved source kinds 0/1.
canonicalForms.arrayArityNotApplicable: Leaf preimages are byte concatenations of a domain string and per-field canonical CBOR fragments, not CBOR arrays, so there is no single array arity. The per-leaf field counts are pinned in exactFields.
canonicalForms.boundary: Script, redeemer, signer, output, output-descriptor, execution, script-context, and resolved-context Merkle leaves that build the validation-machine frontiers consumed by the fraud-proof validators.
canonicalForms.binding: Every leaf builder validates its own arguments before hashing: 28-byte script and signer hashes, 32-byte item commitments and semantic roots, positive script lengths, non-negative indices, and the closed language, purpose, and collection-kind enumerations. TypeScript throws and Aiken fails the `expect` for each violation, so no out-of-range leaf can be produced on either side.
canonicalForms.persistence: Leaves are not persisted individually; they are folded into the logarithmic validation-merkle frontier whose commitment is carried in the on-chain validation-machine control state.

canonicalForms.name: MidgardVersionedScript language tag and script-hash prefix
canonicalForms.kind: closed language enumeration carried as a CBOR array head and as a single hash-prefix byte
canonicalForms.wireRepresentation: Definite CBOR array 0x82 || cbor(language_tag) || definite_bytes(script_bytes). The three admitted tags encode as 0x00 for NativeCardano (0), 0x03 for PlutusV3 (3), and 0x1880 for MidgardV1 (128), so a PlutusV3 witness starts 0x8203 and a MidgardV1 witness starts 0x821880. The script hash is blake2b-224 over the single prefix byte 0x00 / 0x03 / 0x80 concatenated with the script bytes.
canonicalForms.versionPolicy: Tag meanings are preserved rather than renumbered: 0 stays NativeCardano, 3 stays the Cardano PlutusV3 tag, and 128 is the Midgard V1 language. The set is closed at exactly these three values; the hash prefix byte and the CBOR tag are the same number for every language, with 128 shown as 0x80 in the hash preimage and 0x1880 in canonical CBOR.
canonicalForms.constructorTagsNotApplicable: MidgardVersionedScript is a two-item CBOR array, not a Plutus Data constructor. The Aiken MidgardScriptLanguage sum type is mapped to and from the numeric wire tags 0, 3, and 128 by midgard_script_language_from_tag, so the tag values above are the authoritative identity.
canonicalForms.boundary: Script witness preimage (script_tx_wits) and reference-script fields of canonical ledger outputs; the same tag feeds the script-proof source and execution leaves.
canonicalForms.binding: Both sides fail closed on any other tag: Aiken midgard_script_language_from_tag ends in `expect tag == 128`, and the V1 script-proof and validation-machine helpers re-assert `tag == 0 || tag == 3 || tag == 128`; TypeScript decodeMidgardVersionedScript throws "Unsupported Midgard versioned script tag" and then requires a canonical CBOR round trip.
canonicalForms.persistence: Persisted inside the canonical transaction witness-set preimage and inside canonical ledger outputs that carry a reference script, and therefore inside the transaction id, the witness commitment, and the UTxO Merkle root.

canonicalForms.name: Script-source origin-kind dichotomy (inline witness versus reference input)
canonicalForms.kind: two domain-separated leaf shapes selected by a closed origin-kind flag
canonicalForms.wireRepresentation: origin_kind 0 is the inline witness: the source key is the canonical CBOR integer of the script's index in the witness list and the leaf is blake2b_256(MidgardInlineScriptSourceLeafV1 || cbor(source_index) || cbor(language_tag) || definite_bytes(script_hash) || cbor(script_total_length) || definite_bytes(item_commitment)) where item_commitment is the bounded item for raw script field 6. origin_kind 1 is the reference input: the source key is the canonical two-item out-ref CBOR and the leaf is blake2b_256(MidgardScriptSourceLeafV1 || cbor(1) || definite_bytes(source_key) || cbor(language_tag) || definite_bytes(script_hash) || cbor(script_total_length) || definite_bytes(item_commitment)) where item_commitment is the bounded item for ledger-output field 2.
canonicalForms.versionPolicy: Both source kinds are preserved; neither is normalised into the other. The inline variant is keyed by witness index and bound to raw field 6, the reference variant is keyed by the exact ledger out-ref and bound to output field 2, and the two leaf domains differ so an inline source can never impersonate a reference source.
exactFields: inline: 0 source_index, 1 script_language_tag, 2 script_hash (28 bytes), 3 script_total_length, 4 item_commitment (field 6 bounded item, 32 bytes)

reference: 0 constant origin kind 1, 1 source_key (canonical out-ref CBOR, output index <= 65535), 2 script_language_tag, 3 script_hash (28 bytes), 4 script_total_length, 5 item_commitment (field 2 bounded item, 32 bytes)
canonicalForms.constructorTagsNotApplicable: The variants are distinguished by the domain string plus the numeric origin kind 0 or 1, not by a Plutus Data constructor tag. The closed origin-kind set is exactly {0 inline, 1 reference}.
canonicalForms.arrayArityNotApplicable: Source leaves are domain-prefixed hash preimages rather than CBOR arrays; the reference source key inside them is the canonical two-item out-ref array.
canonicalForms.boundary: Script-source resolution during the ScriptSources phase: the resolved reference script recorded in a canonical ledger-output descriptor is folded into the source frontier only when its reference-script language is not absent.

canonicalForms.name: Purpose-kind to redeemer-pointer bijection
canonicalForms.kind: closed bijection between the four V1 purpose kinds and the four admitted redeemer tags
canonicalForms.wireRepresentation: purpose_kind is a small non-negative integer in 0..3 meaning spend, mint, observe, and protected receive. Each maps to exactly one redeemer tag: 0 -> 0, 1 -> 1, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 6. The mapping is total in both directions over those pairs and undefined everywhere else, and a redeemer pointer matches a purpose only when the tag maps back to the purpose kind and redeemer_index equals purpose_index.
canonicalForms.versionPolicy: Purpose meanings are preserved, not renumbered. The Aiken MidgardRedeemerPurpose constructors keep the wider Cardano ordering (Spend 0, Mint 1, Cert 2, Reward 3, Vote 4, Propose 5, Receive 6) while V1 admits only the four tags 0, 1, 3, and 6; the purpose-kind axis 0..3 is the compact consensus ordering used by the proof leaves.
exactFields: pointer match additionally requires redeemer_index == purpose_index
canonicalForms.arrayArityNotApplicable: The bijection is a pair of total functions over small integers, not a CBOR array, so no array arity applies. The purpose leaf that consumes it is a four-field hash preimage pinned in the second canonical form.
canonicalForms.boundary: Script context and proof leaves: the purpose kind selects the script purpose exposed to the program and is committed by the MidgardScriptPurposeLeafV1 leaf, while the redeemer tag and index select the redeemer pointer that must accompany it.
canonicalForms.binding: Both sides return None/null for purpose kinds -1 and 4 and for redeemer tags -1, 2, 4, 5, and 7, and both refuse a pointer whose redeemer index differs from the purpose index, so no unsupported purpose or mismatched pointer can authenticate an execution.
canonicalForms.persistence: Not persisted directly; the redeemer tag and index are persisted inside the canonical redeemer witness preimage and the purpose kind is recomputed and committed into the purpose leaf during a dispute.

canonicalForms.versionPolicy: purpose_kind is constrained to 0..3 and purpose_index to non-negative integers; the script hash is exactly 28 bytes. The field order is frozen for V1.
exactFields: 0: purpose_kind (0 spend | 1 mint | 2 observe | 3 protected receive)

notes: Sole identity owner confirmed mechanically: `computeDeploymentManifestV1Id`, `computeDeploymentManifestV1JsonDigest` and `normalizeDeploymentManifestV1JsonValue` are defined only in demo/midgard-core/src/deployment-manifest-identity-v1.ts. The node re-exports the normalizer and digest verbatim and its `computeDeploymentManifestId` delegates to `computeDeploymentManifestV1Id`; demo/da-committee-node/src/config.ts and demo/midgard-watcher/src (deployment-identity.ts, rule-bundle-v1.ts) import the same core functions. The test `delegates canonical JSON normalization and digesting to core` asserts reference identity (`toBe`) between the node re-exports and the core implementations, so a forked copy would fail.

The node parser is a strict superset check, not a replacement: `parseDeploymentManifestV1Value` first calls core `verifyDeploymentManifestV1Identity` (schemaVersion, exact 18 root keys, profile, profile digest, recomputed manifestId), then runs its own root/nested validation, then calls core `verifyFinalizedDeploymentManifestV1` on the parsed value. Finalized-contract completeness (including the mandatory fraud-proof catalogue and the `steps.prepareHubOracleNonce/deployNodeRuntimeReferenceScripts/initProtocol` must-be-complete rule) therefore always runs even though the node's own `validateContracts` treats `fraudProofCatalogue` as an optional key.

Hostile recomputed-ID tampering is covered specifically: `rejects tampered script bytes even with a recomputed manifest ID`, `rejects catalogue root, positional ID, and membership-proof tampering`, `rejects a deployment manifest with an unknown network` and both da-committee-node `withRecomputedDeploymentManifestId` cases all recompute a self-consistent manifestId and still fail on the semantic binding.
The producer cannot emit an unparsed manifest: `buildDeploymentManifestV1` returns `parseDeploymentManifestV1Value(manifest)`, so construction and reading share one language.

`demo/midgard-core/tests/deployment-manifest-identity-v1.test.ts` and `demo/midgard-node/tests/midgard-contracts.test.ts` contain further direct coverage of the core identity owner and the runtime contract reconstruction path, but neither file is in the passed-test index, so neither is cited.

Core-side first-party coverage of the sole identity owner is cited directly: `recomputes the exact full-manifest identity` pins a golden manifestId vector for `computeDeploymentManifestV1Id`, and `rejects tampering, missing fields, and extra fields` rejects a network mutation (id mismatch), a missing root member, and an extra `historicalVersion` key at `verifyDeploymentManifestV1Identity`.

The only chain-facing bytes they reference (the PHAS stake-registration CBOR) are re-derived with CML rather than encoded by any Aiken type, so no Plutus datum or redeemer carries these formats.

notes: Ten distinct exact V1 forms are retained: environment artifact and environment document, local genesis-ledger report, T1 probe, T1 canonical advance, T1 recovery attestation, PHAS registration proof, both PHAS transaction-body shapes, and the pipelined-commit process-acceptance summary.

midgard-phas-registration-transaction-body-v1 names two different exact shapes at two boundaries: the node-built evidence {schemaVersion,txHash,cborSha256,cborSizeBytes,certificate} in src/transactions/phas-membership-registration.ts and the cardano-cli member {schemaVersion,artifactSha256,cborSha256,cborSizeBytes,cardanoCliTxHash,certificate} nested in the PHAS registration proof. Each decoder rejects the other's key set, so both are listed as separate canonical forms under one identity string.

midgard-phase4-t1-recovery-attestation-v1 and midgard-phase4-phas-registration-proof-v1 are each validated twice by independent implementations (the TypeScript command/controller and the standalone .mjs summary verifier) that enforce the same key sets.

Further parameterized rejection cases exist as it.each blocks ("rejects adversarial report mutation %#" in the genesis-ledger suite and "rejects unsafe identity %#" for its gate); they are not cited individually because only the parameterized title text appears literally in the source file.

crossLanguageEvidence.notApplicableReason: The consolidation journal, result, report, and readiness evidence are local operator-side JSON/NDJSON files under the node's .stress-wallets directory; no Plutus datum, redeemer, or Aiken type encodes them, and the only on-chain-shaped value they carry (the signed Midgard native V1 transaction CBOR) is cross-checked against the shared midgard-core codec rather than against a separate Aiken encoding.

notes: The retired identity midgard-stress-wallet-consolidate-v1 was grepped (grep -rn -F) against every path the A13-A16-retired-stress-artifacts scan covers - demo/midgard-node/src/commands/stress-wallets.ts, stress-corpus-generate.ts, the stress-corpus/ directory, stress-open-loop.ts, and demo/midgard-node/scripts/throughput-valid-stress-corpus.mjs - with zero matches; the only occurrence anywhere in demo/ is as a rejected input literal in demo/midgard-node/tests/stress-wallets.test.ts, where parseStressWalletConsolidationJournal is asserted to throw `Unsupported consolidation state schema` for it.

midgard-stress-wallet-consolidation-result-v1 has direct positive coverage only (parseStressWalletConsolidationResult is asserted to accept the produced result, never asserted to throw). Its rejection surface is exercised indirectly and completely: parseStressWalletConsolidationReport reuses the same STRESS_WALLET_CONSOLIDATION_RESULT_KEYS exact-key list and the same parseStressWalletConsolidationResultFields accounting validator, and that parser is asserted to throw for a wrong schemaVersion, an extra root key, and an extra nested key.

The consolidation readiness identity is claimed here rather than in A14: the literal is midgard-stress-wallet-consolidation-readiness-v1, it is produced and consumed only inside the consolidate command path, and A13's canonical text explicitly enumerates journal, result, report, and readiness evidence.

notes: Per-identity green coverage. midgard-stress-wallet-v1: positive and rejection in `creates persisted L2 wallet records and redacted command output` (accepts the persisted record, rejects an extra `historical` key, a missing seedPhrase, and midgard-stress-wallet-v2), plus a second independent reader covered by `projects only canonical wallet funding semantics`. midgard-stress-wallet-create-result-v1: positive and rejection in `creates persisted L2 wallet records and redacted command output` (extra root key, broken cardinality binding, extra nested wallet key). midgard-stress-wallet-prepare-result-v1: positive and rejection in `prepares wallets by skipping funded records, depositing missing funds, projecting, and verifying /utxos` (prepare-result-v2, missing wallets, extra nested key). midgard-stress-wallet-fanout-result-v1 and midgard-stress-wallet-fanout-report-v1: positive and rejection in `fans out L2 funding level-by-level and records verified funding snapshots` (extra root key on the result, extra edge key on the report). midgard-stress-wallet-terminal-drain-journal-v1 and midgard-stress-wallet-terminal-drain-report-v1: positive and rejection in `prepares every terminal drain before submission and resumes exact CBOR to zero with private conservation evidence` (terminal-drain-v1 identity, extra root key, missing entries, tampered scopeSha256, tampered txHash/CBOR/selectedInputs, extra nested conservation key).

Honest gap: midgard-stress-wallet-terminal-drain-result-v1 has direct positive coverage only. parseStressWalletTerminalDrainResult is asserted to accept both the prepared-phase and the committed-phase result, but no green test calls it with a mutated document and asserts a throw, and its STRESS_WALLET_TERMINAL_DRAIN_RESULT_KEYS list is not shared with any other parser. Its phase/cardinality and conservation invariants are nevertheless exercised end-to-end at the producer boundary: `rejects a nonempty zero-value residual UTxO and a treasury conservation mismatch` drives terminalDrainStressWallets to fail closed on exact-zero conservation before the result can be produced, and `rejects every non-canonical already_empty variant before status, submission, or journal rewrite` plus `keeps the prepare-all barrier on partial failure and rejects a CAS mutation without submission` cover the prepared-phase barrier. A direct one-line mutation test on parseStressWalletTerminalDrainResult would close this cleanly.

crossLanguageEvidence.notApplicableReason: The corpus manifest, generation result, verification artifact, prefix evidence, index rows, and corpus rows are offline benchmark-input files on the operator's filesystem; no Aiken type or Plutus datum/redeemer encodes any of them. The cross-language concern they do carry - that every corpus row's bytes really are a canonical Midgard native V1 transaction - is discharged by decoding each row through the shared midgard-core codec and recomputing its transaction id, so the on-chain-relevant encoding is checked against the single canonical implementation rather than against a parallel Aiken definition.

notes: Per-identity green coverage. midgard-stress-corpus-generation-v1: positive and rejection in `generates, assembles, manifests, and verifies a grouped chain corpus` (accepts the produced artifact; rejects midgard-stress-corpus-generation-v0, a missing `verified` block, a missing plan.amountLovelace, an extra root key, and two distinct broken result bindings), plus a second standalone reader in `verification evidence binds corpus, index, counts, and rebuild sample`. midgard-stress-corpus-manifest-v1: positive and rejection in the same TypeScript test (legacy-v2 schemaVersion, missing files, extra root key, non-canonical generatedAtIso, and four distinct cardinality-binding violations) and independently in `rejects incomplete, extra-key, and wrong-version corpus manifests` against the standalone reader. midgard-stress-corpus-verification-v1: positive and rejection in the same TypeScript test (midgard-stress-corpus-verification-v0, missing corpus.manifestSha256, extra nested key). midgard-stress-corpus-prefix-evidence-v1: positive in `binds full SHA, cardinality, uniqueness, manifest, and source identity`, rejection in `rejects corpus rows, indices, and prefix evidence with non-exact keys` (extra key) and in `detects same-size corpus replacement with restored mtime in consumed-prefix evidence` (byte drift under an identical size and restored mtime).

Two of the six canonical forms - StressCorpusNdjsonIndexEntry and StressCorpusNdjsonRow - deliberately have no `midgard-...-v1` schemaVersion field. Their identity is the closed exact-key set plus the digest binding from the enclosing manifest/generation documents. They are listed as forms because the row's requiredEvidence explicitly demands index/row and canonical native row/hash/outref checks; the audit `identities` list for this row names only the four versioned string identities.

Divergence worth recording (not a blocker): the two independent reimplementations of the index-row shape disagree on one bound. parseStressCorpusIndexLine in demo/midgard-node/src/commands/stress-corpus/verify.ts requires endByteOffset > startByteOffset strictly, while loadCorpusIndex in demo/midgard-node/scripts/throughput-valid-stress-corpus.mjs only rejects endByteOffset < startByteOffset, so the standalone reader would accept a zero-length range that the TypeScript reader rejects. Both readers still bind the file digest, and no producer emits a zero-length range (assembleCorpusShards only writes runs with rowCount > 0), so this is a strictness asymmetry rather than an accepted-format difference.

demo/midgard-node/scripts/mpf-architecture-g-corpus.mjs is cited as an additional standalone JavaScript reader bound to the midgard-stress-corpus-generation-v1 identity literal. It is a narrowing projection over the verified/rebuildSample subtree (validateCanonicalCorpusVerificationEvidence), not a full exact-key parser; the authoritative exact parser remains parseStressCorpusGenerationArtifactV1.

crossLanguageEvidence.notApplicableReason: All twelve Architecture G identities are process-local benchmark evidence produced by demo/midgard-node scripts and workers and persisted as JSON files or stdout lines on the measurement host. No Aiken validator, Plutus datum, or redeemer encodes a root-gate summary, corpus-preparation artifact, funding map, candidate seed/input, seed result, probe result, or candidate gate summary, so there is no on-chain or Aiken counterpart to cross-check.

notes: All twelve required identities are literally present in active source: phase1-formal-binding-identity and runtime-identity in mpf-architecture-g-gate-config.mjs and src/workers/utils/mpf-commit-candidate-artifacts.ts; corpus-preparation, corpus-funding, production-root-gate and root-diagnostic-smoke produced in mpf-architecture-g-gate.mjs; commit-candidate-seed and commit-candidate-input produced in mpf-architecture-g-candidate-input.mjs; commit-candidate-seed-result in src/workers/mpf-commit-candidate-seed.ts; commit-candidate-probe in src/workers/mpf-commit-candidate-probe.ts; commit-candidate-gate and commit-candidate-smoke in mpf-architecture-g-commit-candidate-gate.mjs and mpf-architecture-g-candidate-summary.mjs.

The formal/smoke pairs (production-root-gate vs root-diagnostic-smoke, commit-candidate-gate vs commit-candidate-smoke) share one validator and one root key language; the identity is selected by the strict boolean `formal` flag, and each validator rejects a document that carries the other profile's schemaVersion.

phase1-formal-binding-identity-v1 and runtime-identity-v1 have no standalone file of their own: they are always nested inside another Architecture G artifact, and both the .mjs validator and the TypeScript decoder re-check them at every embedding boundary.

Oversize and substitution rejection is asserted directly: funding outputCbor at 1048576+ hex chars, seed-input paths at 4096+ chars and paths containing NUL, symlinked source files and symlinked traversal roots, and untracked files appearing after the root gate.

crossLanguageEvidence.notApplicableReason: Both identities are host-side operational diagnostics of the Architecture G benchmark run: a redacted driver-log scan record embedded in a local JSON report, and a Docker load-container supervision NDJSON stream written on the benchmark host. Neither is ever submitted to a chain, and no Aiken validator, Plutus datum, or redeemer encodes or reads a secret-scan result or a watchdog event, so there is no cross-language counterpart.

notes: Redaction happens strictly before persistence: createSecretScanningLog is line-buffered and writes the fixed `[REDACTED secret-bearing driver output]` marker instead of any line matching the sensitive-label or long-hex/base64 patterns, and instead of any line exceeding 65536 chars; the retained bytes are asserted never to contain the secret value.

Clean-result enforcement lives in the consumer: validateSecretScannedLog requires passed === true with zero sensitive and zero oversized lines, so a scan that merely reports its own failure cannot promote a report.

The watchdog's contiguity guarantee is two-sided: createEvidenceWriter assigns the next sequence itself and passes it as the expected sequence to the canonicalizer, and parseThroughputWatchdogEvidenceLineV1 requires the caller-supplied expected sequence to match on read-back; the oversized-diagnostic test walks all nine emitted lines and asserts sequence === index + 1.

Immutable target identity is enforced across the whole lifecycle: the container is only accepted while `created` and not running with the required label, is re-inspected for identical ID/state/label after preflight before start, and every stop, kill, and verification action is issued against the captured ID rather than the caller-supplied name.
